verdict.rationale: The evidence supports JMAP as an open, fully documented standard tied to Fastmail's API documentation and open-standards page. Hands-on community use confirms SMTP access via an app password. However, IMAP client access is only implied by a migration comment, and standards-based export is not evidenced at all. Missing for 10: explicit first-party docs for IMAP/SMTP client access, documented standards-based export (e.g., mbox/EML, vCard/iCal), Fastmail-specific JMAP endpoint documentation beyond page titles.

support.subject: As a switcher, my mail stays reachable over open protocols and standard formats — IMAP/JMAP/SMTP access and standards-based export — so no client can lock me in

citations.quote: JMAP is an open standard any organisation can implement, not more proprietary lock-in from big tech companies.
No patents. No fees. Fully documented. JMAP is an open standard any organisation can implement
Uses Fastmail SMTP for transactional emails with an app password that can only access SMTP.
